one_liner: HubSpot has a broad REST API with OAuth2 and service key/private app tokens, free developer accounts, webhooks, and an official remote MCP server.
auth_notes: OAuth 2.0 authorization code required for multi-account apps; access tokens expire in 30 minutes with refresh tokens. Service keys and static app/private-app tokens serve single-account use.
access_notes: Free developer account with test accounts and API access; every plan including free CRM has API access. Rate limits vary by tier (100 calls/10s on Free/Starter).
blocker_notes: Minor: installing an app requires a Super Admin; legacy private apps are being deprecated; dated API versioning needs tracking.

evidence.quote: HubSpot supports the [OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code grant type]
you can use service keys to query HubSpot’s [REST APIs](/docs/api-reference/latest/overview) directly without having to use the CLI or other platform developer tools first.

There are two ways to authenticate calls to HubSpot’s APIs: [OAuth](/docs/apps/legacy-apps/authentication/working-with-oauth), and [private app](/docs/apps/legacy-apps/private-apps/overview) access tokens.
You can create a free HubSpot account and build apps without a paid subscription.
Every HubSpot plan has it, including the free CRM, and API calls cost no extra fee.
The API is a set of web addresses at api.hubapi.com, one family per object, with the data as JSON.
You can create up to 1,000 [webhook subscriptions](/docs/api-reference/latest/webhooks) per app.
The remote HubSpot MCP server is a publicly hosted endpoint for connecting external AI tools and applications to HubSpot’s CRM.
Configuring your MCP client to connect to the HubSpot MCP server at `https://mcp.hubspot.com` using your connector’s OAuth credentials.
